scope: PNG-only native1024 review of every gray image016–031. No images removed/reordered, no model imports, loads, inference, source edits or quality approval. Observations concern appearance, not real identity/gender/ethnicity or actual age.
cohort: Unfiltered fresh32 NADA500; this review covers second16 only.
sampling: psi1, constant noise, no restoration or output selection
summary: Main heads and faces are generally coherent in this half, unlike the architecture-over-face failures of the earlier reference256 sample. This is a cross-model, different-seed observation, not a matched quality measurement.

All16 display a learned white neck band/bib. It is usually very broad, smooth and directly attached to the jaw; none demonstrates the requested crisp small Roman tab inside naturally constructed black shirt. Clerical semantics emerging is real visual evidence, but collar quality is not solved.

There are clear hats at017/023/027, definite additional partial heads at020/021, and a possible background person at029.022/027 are not clearly adult,028 looks like a child. Stubble does not establish adulthood.

Some adult faces could fit the calendar aesthetic, especially016/024/030;021/023 have potentially attractive central faces but fail extra-person/headwear requirements. The subjective candidate label is not an image-quality pass. No attractiveness assessment is made for apparent children or age-uncertain faces.

Skin, eyes, lips and teeth remain soft, mottled or etched at native1024. Several faces share a stubbled, mildly smiling family resemblance despite varied hair/accessories; this is a diversity concern, not a measured identity-collapse conclusion.
A restoration diagnostic could test soft intact faces, but cannot be presumed to remove hats, other people, youthful appearance or unconvincing collar construction. No production approval.
